column1: # Worked-example acronym registry (@PLN141) — maps a tag acronym to the repo that
# owns it, so a `// Example: @AAA-###` citation resolves to a real test/function and
# produces a real link.  Tab-separated:  acronym <TAB> repo <TAB> git_url <TAB> branch
# Projects are assumed to be checked out as SIBLINGS in one parent directory, so the
# local checkout is simply `../<repo>` — no per-entry path navigation.  A present
# sibling is validated OFFLINE against its checkout (preferred over online); a missing
# one is reported unvalidated (a warning, never a hard failure), with the link still
# emitted from git_url.  The acronym namespace is ecosystem-global: one acronym names
# MONOREPO libraries: several packages share one git repo (e.g. loft-libs-graphics
# holds graphics + gridmesh + shapes).  The `repo` column is that monorepo's checkout
# dir (`../loft-libs-graphics`), so multiple acronyms map to it — the gate scans the
# whole tree for the acronym's `// @AAA-###` tag and emits a repo-relative blob link
# (`.../blob/main/gridmesh/tests/x.loft#L12`), so no per-package path column is needed.
# The rows below stake the ecosystem-global acronym claim so no other repo reuses them.
# The distributed LIBRARIES are loft's to roll out (shared code, each guarded by its own
# validated contract); the first-class APPS (DRY/CRW/MOR) are their own agents' to author
# — loft only CITES those.  Which acronyms carry tags today: each repo's examples-index.tsv.
